resume: Length of the leave, notice periods for your employer, daily allowances and documents to send to the Assurance Maladie, plus the new additional birth leave.
aQuoiCaSert: Paternity and childcare leave (congé de paternité et d'accueil de l'enfant) allows the father, or the mother's spouse, PACS partner (civil partnership) or cohabiting partner, to stop working after the birth to look after the child. During this leave, the employment contract is suspended and the Assurance Maladie (French public health insurance; in French Guiana, the CGSS) may pay daily allowances. Since July 1, 2026, an additional birth leave can be added.
quiEstConcerne: The mother's spouse, PACS partner or cohabiting partner, if not the father.
These pages concern the private sector: civil servants, self-employed people and other schemes have their own rules.
aSavoir: Separated parents: the child's father is entitled to it with no requirement of marriage, PACS or living with the mother. The requirement to live as a couple only applies to a spouse or partner who is not the father.
Length: 25 calendar days for a birth (32 for multiple births), in addition to the 3-working-day birth leave. A 4-day period is mandatory right after the birth leave.
The remaining 21 days (28 for multiple births) can be taken all at once or in 2 periods of at least 5 days, within 6 months of the birth.

Tell your employer at least 1 month before the expected date of delivery, then at least 1 month before the start of each period, stating the dates and length. Doing so in writing is advised: registered letter with acknowledgment of receipt, or hand delivery against a signed receipt.

Daily allowances: among other conditions, you must have been registered for at least 6 months and have worked 150 hours in the previous 3 months, or paid contributions on at least €12,058.20 of salary over 6 months. They range from €11.12 to €104.02 per day (service-public.gouv.fr, checked as of June 1, 2026).

Additional birth leave: since July 1, 2026, each parent can take 1 to 2 months of paid leave after maternity or paternity leave. For an employee, the allowance is 70% of net salary the first month and 60% the second, up to the social security ceiling. Tell your employer at least 1 month in advance (code.travail.gouv.fr).
